$comment: Hand-authored ground truth for synthetic_instrument_v1.txt (see README.md — this is synthetic fixture data, not real regulatory text). Keyed by structural_path (article-N/paragraph-M), which matches the suffix of the pipeline's own deterministically-derived anchor_id, so labels don't need to be re-derived if document_id/source_version change between runs. 26 clauses across 6 articles: 19 genuinely normative, 3 planted false positives (modal verb present but not a real obligation), 4 true negatives (no modal verb at all).
$core_field_matching_note: expected_core_fields.action/object are genuinely-correct short phrases, authored by reading each clause's text — NOT tuned to match clause_parser/src/agents/extraction_agent.py's actual output. That fixture's action field is literally the entire verbatim sentence (span_text.strip()[:200]) and its object field is literally the structural anchor_label (e.g. 'Article 1(1)') — neither is a real semantic extraction. Matching is EXACT (case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized), deliberately not lenient/substring-based, so core-field F1 honestly reflects that this fixture extractor has no real action/object extraction capability, only actor/modality pattern-matching. A low F1 on action/object is the correct, expected result of this fixture, not a harness bug.
$complex_field_matching_note: expected_complex_fields (conditions/exceptions/deadline_iso/related_articles) are genuinely-correct values, authored independently of extraction_agent.py's/resolver.py's actual regex-based logic. Two clauses (article-1/paragraph-1, article-4/paragraph-1) use a TRAILING 'main-clause, where X' condition pattern that the extractor's condition regex does not handle (it only recognizes a LEADING 'Where X, and where Y, main-clause' chain) — their expected conditions are populated anyway and are EXPECTED to legitimately score as a miss, not a harness bug. article-1/paragraph-3's expected deadline_iso ('P30D') is similarly expected to miss: the action field's 200-character truncation of the verbatim sentence cuts off 'within 30 days' before the deadline regex ever sees it. Both are real, documented fixture limitations, not corpus/harness errors — see clause_parser/src/agents/extraction_agent.py and resolver.py's own comments for the underlying cause.

conditions: the incident has a material impact on service continuity

article-1/paragraph-1.notes: Baseline normative obligation. Trailing condition pattern the extractor doesn't capture (see $complex_field_matching_note).

article-1/paragraph-2.notes: No modal verb; background/purpose text only.

conditions: the affected product has already been recalled under a separate procedure

article-1/paragraph-3.notes: Compound leading conditions. Deadline is expected to miss (200-char action truncation cuts off 'within 30 days' — see $complex_field_matching_note).

exceptions: the incident has already been reported to the competent authority under Article 1(1)

article-1/paragraph-4.notes: Exception references a specific earlier clause by number (cross-reference + exception combined).

article-1/paragraph-5.notes: Contains 'should' but explicitly disclaims imposing any independent obligation — a naive keyword detector is EXPECTED to mis-flag this as normative.

article-2/paragraph-1.notes: References Article 1(1) by number; the referenced clause is not adjacent.

article-2/paragraph-2.notes: Exemption condition, not an obligation; no modal verb of its own.

article-2/paragraph-3.notes: Contains 'shall' only in a definitional sense ('X shall mean...'), not as an obligation — planted false positive.

exceptions: retention is prohibited by another applicable law

article-2/paragraph-4.notes: 'except where X' — regression-tested to NOT also be double-counted as a condition (see extraction_agent.py's _CONDITION_RE fix).

expected_core_fields.action: be protected against unauthorised access using industry-standard encryption

article-2/paragraph-5.notes: Two obligations in one sentence (protect + review annually); passive voice, no controlled-vocabulary actor named, so 'unspecified_actor' is the genuinely correct actor value here.

expected_core_fields.action: implement appropriate technical and organisational measures

article-3/paragraph-3.notes: Savings/non-derogation clause — does not impose an obligation on any actor, despite containing 'should'. Planted false positive.

conditions: the essential entity operates in more than one Member State
the relevant competent authorities have not agreed on a lead authority

exceptions: the competent authority has waived this requirement in writing

article-3/paragraph-5.notes: Two obligations (assess + report) plus a deadline and an exception in one sentence.

conditions: the incident has a material impact on service continuity

article-4/paragraph-1.notes: Amends Article 1(1)'s deadline from 72 to 24 hours — exercises AMENDS (§3.2: Provision->Provision) once mapped to the graph. Trailing condition pattern the extractor doesn't capture, same as article-1/paragraph-1.

expected_core_fields.object: the cybersecurity risk posed by its direct suppliers and service providers

article-5/paragraph-1.notes: Baseline supply-chain obligation. 'service providers' contains the controlled-vocabulary substring 'provider', so the fixture actor extractor genuinely (correctly, per its own substring-match design) also returns 'provider' alongside 'important entity'.

conditions: a supplier has previously been subject to a significant incident
exceptions: the supplier has since obtained independent security certification

article-5/paragraph-2.notes: Both a leading condition AND a trailing exception in the same sentence.

article-5/paragraph-3.notes: Explicitly disclaims imposing any obligation; no modal verb.

expected_core_fields.action: require its suppliers to notify it

article-5/paragraph-4.notes: Hour-based deadline (exercises the PT#H ISO-8601 time-designator fix).

article-5/paragraph-5.notes: Two obligations (audits + cooperation) plus an exception; passive voice, no controlled-vocabulary actor named.

expected_core_fields.object: training to gain sufficient knowledge and skills

article-6/paragraph-2.notes: 'Members of the management body' is not in the controlled vocabulary, so 'unspecified_actor' is the genuinely correct actor value.

article-6/paragraph-4.notes: Scope-limiting exclusion clause; no modal verb of its own.

conditions: the essential entity is part of a group
the parent undertaking has already approved equivalent measures at group level
exceptions: a competent authority objects in writing within 30 days

article-6/paragraph-5.notes: Last paragraph in the document, immediately followed by two Annexes — regression-tested to confirm its span/verbatim_text does NOT swallow the trailing annex content (see canonicalizer.py's document_ceiling fix). Compound leading conditions plus a trailing exception plus two cross-references.

annex_note: Annex I and Annex II are present in the raw text for lexical/annotation purposes but are NOT structurally recognized as distinct 'annex' anchor types by this synthetic fixture's canonicalizer pass — clause_parser/src/canonicalize/canonicalizer.py currently only detects 'Article N' / numbered-paragraph patterns (see that module's own docstring: 'unmatched text becomes a single top-level article anchor... extending its coverage is future work'). Tracked as a corpus/parser coverage gap, not silently ignored. A related, more severe consequence (the LAST article's last paragraph silently swallowing trailing annex text into its own evidence) was found and FIXED separately — see canonicalizer.py's document_ceiling / _ANNEX_HEADING_RE.
